Subject: Proposal: safety-band adjustment for Dedicated pilot (PulseAI) — canary request

Team —

Quick summary: PulseAI (enterprise pilot, high-throughput embeddings/semantic-search) is asking for a short-term uplift to their Dedicated pool reservation. They want the safety buffer (our default idle/reserve band) reduced from 20% to 10% for a 30-day pilot window to achieve target p95 tail latency during peak ingestion. Sales/AE have flagged this as a make-or-break ask for the pilot contract.

Why I'm raising this here: changing the safety band is an infra & policy-level exception. I want product, infra, and ops alignment on a low-risk canary we can run that preserves SLAs for other tenants while giving PulseAI the headroom they want.

Proposal (high-level):
- Scope: one Dedicated pool in us-west-2 tag=pilot-pulse — 30-day window starting 2028-05-20.
- Safety band change: reduce reserved safety band from 20% -> 10% for that pool only.
- Controls: automatic circuit breaker if aggregate pool utilization > 92% for more than 5m or if customer p95 latency > 750ms.
- Observability: add token-level cost/latency dashboard, alert to oncall and to product.
- Rollback: immediate rollback to 20% if circuit trips, with automated notification and a follow-up post-mortem.

Ask of you all:
- Marcus: can infra/ops implement the circuit-breaker and confirm rollback automation + monitor metrics we need?
- Laura: any product constraints (model rollout collision, autoprioritization) we should know about?
- Grace: legal/CS implications for an SLA deviation and how we should message Pulse?

I attached a one-page proposal and a draft ops runbook. If we can agree, I want to run a 2-week canary (05/20–06/03) and then give the customer the remainder if all looks healthy.

Thanks —
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Kim — thanks for the clear ask and proposal. A few operational notes from infra/ops perspective: 

1) Circuit breaker: we can implement rate-based and utilization-based breakers, but we need concrete thresholds and an owner for alerts. The 92% utilization trigger seems reasonable as a starting point; suggest we also add a per-GPU memory pressure metric (eviction risk) as a secondary signal.

2) Telemetry: to be safe we'll need the following visible in Grafana/Tracing within the first 24h of the canary: pool aggregate utilization, per-customer token rate, model kv-cache hit rate, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and number of prefix cache evictions. Without those we can't approve a lowered safety band.

3) Rollback automation: we have tooling to flip pool safety band atomically, but that change must be gated by an ops runbook: who executes, who confirms, and the communication template to customers. I can have an initial automation ready by 05/18, but the runbook steps need a named oncall.

4) Risk: if another enterprise pool collides (scheduled load test, PS workload) we WILL see contention. Recommend we block scheduled large jobs (training/cold-start sweeps) against the physical cluster during the canary window, and we should temporarily disable soft-burst across affected pools.

I can own the automation and monitoring items if we name an oncall and lock the canary window.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Infra & Runtime

Kim / Marcus —

Thanks for the quick start. A few product-side considerations: 

- Model rollout collisions: PulseAI will be testing two model variants during the pilot. If we change safety bands, we need to ensure their canary doesn't interact with our global canary sweeps (we have a sweep scheduled 05/25 for a new quantized LLM profile). Recommend we either (a) move the product sweep by one week, or (b) scope PulseAI's models to the pilot pool only and disable global canary routing for those requests. Option (b) is preferable to avoid global impact.

- Billing/credits: if we reduce safety band, the effective utilization changes and so does unit economics. Sales/legal should confirm billing treatment (pro-rated credit vs. committed tier).

- UX: if circuit trips and we rollback, we should surface a clear message in the customer console explaining the reason and next steps. Ops should provide the exact message copy for CS.

I can coordinate product side and will own the collision mitigation (option b) if infra can scope routing.

-Laura
Principal PM, Serving
